releases.notes:
Adds Minecraft **26.3** support, porting the client render path onto the API that replaced
Blaze3D ("RenderPearl"): pipelines, bind group layouts, GPU buffers/textures, `RenderPass`
and the shader plumbing all moved or changed shape, and 26.3 draws translucent terrain
through an order-independent-transparency pipeline set while chunk layers gained a second,
multi-draw-indirect pipeline. All of it is version-gated in the same source tree, so **26.2
still builds and runs** from this release too.

**Fixed along the way** (every one of these came out of actually running the client, not
from reading code):

- Layers using `blend=replace` crashed on their first frame - a pipeline has to declare a
  colour target state even when nothing is blended.
- The sky cube rendered nothing on 26.3: its inward-facing quads were culled under the new
  winding convention.
- Entering a world crashed with `IndexOutOfBoundsException` when options.txt still held the
  toggle key's pre-26.3 binding (`key.keyboard.-1`) - 26.3 moved
  `InputConstants.UNKNOWN` from keysym -1 to key 0. A stale binding is now dropped at
  startup.
- A pack whose texture names mix case (e.g. ICY's `Sunset2a.png`) made the resource reload
  throw, which made Minecraft drop *every* selected pack instead of just that layer. The
  layer is now skipped with a warning naming the file, and the rest of the pack loads.

**Verified in-game on 26.3** with two real custom sky packs: ICY (5 of its 7 layers load -
one has a 24-hour fade window, one references `Sunset2a.png`) and Stimpy WAR Eum3 Revamp
(all 4 layers load). Day, night, starfield and the fog-blending modes all render.

**Requirements**
- Minecraft 26.3
- Fabric Loader 0.19.3+
- Fabric API 0.161.0+26.3
- Mod Menu 21.0.0 (optional, only used for the settings screen)

The `+26.2` jar is attached as well, for anyone still on 26.2 (Fabric API 0.156.0+26.2,
Mod Menu 20.0.1).

releases.notes:
Fixes underwater (and lava/powder-snow) fog incorrectly picking up the **Fog Blending**
setting from v1.1.0 - terrain fog while submerged now correctly stays the vanilla tinted
water fog color instead of fading toward the custom sky.

**Under the hood:** build migrated to [Stonecutter](https://stonecutter.kikugie.dev/) to
prepare multi-version support (1.21.11/26.1/26.2) from one source tree. Only 26.2 builds
for now; 1.21.11/26.1 need further porting work for Blaze3D rendering API changes.

**Requirements**
- Minecraft 26.2
- Fabric Loader 0.19.3+
- Fabric API

releases.notes:
Adds a **Fog Blending** setting (Vanilla / Directional / Per-Pixel) that lets distant fog
match the active custom sky instead of always fading to the dimension's flat vanilla color:

- **Vanilla** - unchanged fog, ignores the custom sky.
- **Directional** - fog fades toward a single color sampled from the custom sky in the
  direction you're facing.
- **Per-Pixel** - terrain fog samples the actual custom sky per-pixel, so it matches what's
  really behind it in every direction. Default.

Configurable from the mod's settings screen (Mod Menu), with tooltips explaining the
tradeoffs of each mode.

**Requirements**
- Minecraft 26.2
- Fabric Loader 0.19.3+
- Fabric API
